options.overgrown_vegetation.show_all_fe: Draws fern fronds folded along their midrib (two planes per frond). When off, each frond is a single flat plane, roughly halving the face count (all 6 fronds are drawn either way). Overgrown terrain is packed with undergrowth, so this is the biggest single FPS factor.
gui.overgrown_vegetation.world_difficult: Enables features that are still unfinished. Currently: the new Nether corruption (roots that run from the portal exit to the lava sea, a forest that turns hot ground into wetland over five stages, pioneer plants, tube trees, lakes and Nether spores). While off, the Nether only changes through ordinary corruption (mobs and so on) turning blocks into their overgrown forms. You can switch it later: turning it off pauses the forest and leaves already changed blocks in place; turning it back on resumes where it stopped.
gui.overgrown_vegetation.gameplay_settin: Gameplay settings are per world. Open them inside a world (the sapling button on the pause screen) or while creating a world (the sapling button next to Difficulty).
gui.overgrown_vegetation.world_difficult: These values apply only to this world and take effect immediately.
These values apply only to the world being created. You can change them later while playing.
View only. Only operators can change these on this server.
Only operators can change the Overgrown Vegetation settings.

This mod's own difficulty, separate from Minecraft's. Choosing a level sets the items marked in green (the 4 mob strength values, phase progress, forest budget income and cap, exposure build-up and infection progress) to Easy 70% / Normal 100% / Hard 150% / Nightmare 300%, and clears per-mob details. Changing any of them makes it Custom.
Items marked ※ do not undo what has already happened when changed mid-game.
Changed together by the mod difficulty level.
Applies to every mob. Changing this clears the per-mob details for this value so all mobs match it. Also applies to mobs already in the world.
Some mobs use their own value
How fast blight ferns, corrupted corpses and raid corruption spread into nearby blocks. Also set by /ov corruption speed.
How many phase points are gained (time, spread, mobs killed, advancements, forest organs). At 0% the phase never advances.
When on, distant land with no players also becomes overgrown (including the End island). When off, only loaded chunks. Off makes the overgrown area grow slower and phases advance slower.
Days until the first quake (start of phase 1). The quake happens once this many days have passed and the advancement count below is reached.
Number of different advancements (by anyone) needed for the first quake. 0 means days only.
How fast the forest (its director) gains the budget (biomass) it spends on spawning mobs and raids.
How much budget (biomass) the forest can store. Larger means bigger attacks at once.
Max attackers at once in a large raid
During the forest's large raid, the most plant-side mobs (attackers) around a base at the same time. Killed ones are replaced right away even at the cap. Higher is heavier.
Max health of this mod's mobs (except ambient creatures).
Damage this mod's mobs (except ambient creatures) deal to living things, including indirect attacks such as projectiles and explosions.
Armor of this mod's mobs (except ambient creatures). Mobs with 0 armor stay at 0. Capped at 30.
Armor toughness of this mod's mobs (except ambient creatures), which softens strong hits. Mobs with 0 stay at 0. Capped at 20.
How fast a player's spore exposure builds up (breathing, seeping from rooms or dirty gear, wounds and skills).
How fast an infected player's infection stage advances.
gui.overgrown_vegetation.visual_settings: These look and sound settings apply to this computer only (the same in every world). They take effect on Done.
Sets the atmosphere quality and curled ferns to this preset. Changing one of them afterwards makes it Custom. The effect switches below are not touched.
Medium: for a GTX 1650 class card
High: for an RTX 4060 class card
Turns all of the overgrown jungle's effects (ambient sound, light, fog, particles, underwater light) on or off. Off turns every switch below off too. Affects performance (off is the lightest).
Number of light shafts, sunflecks and glowing particles, and how fine the fog is. Affects performance. Fog detail is drawn only at High.
Shape of the curled fern. Detailed = folded fronds (86 faces), Standard = 6 flat fronds (42 faces). Affects performance. Same setting as Detailed Fern Fronds in Video Settings.
gui.overgrown_vegetation.world_difficult: The phase never advances past this. Lowering it does not bring the current phase back.
When on, corruption creeps up placed buildings. When off, buildings are not covered (corruption still comes from the ground).
Spread to the Nether and End
When corruption reaches a portal frame, the forest crosses into the Nether or End. When off it does not (forest already there stays).
Blocks within this many blocks of the Overworld spawn point are never corrupted. 0 = none. Already corrupted blocks do not revert.
How often nurseries ask the forest to hatch a mob. Whether one hatches still depends on the forest budget.
When off, no new organs grow. Existing organs stay.
Multiplies the per-phase cap on organs. Lowering it does not remove existing organs.
When off, giant trees do not grow in newly generated land or from saplings. Existing giant trees stay.
When off, the forest sends no raids at bases (normal, saved-up or large).
How often raid chances come. 200% halves the gap.
Multiplier on the number of mobs in a normal (small) raid.
Multiplier on the number of mobs in a slightly saved-up (medium) raid.
Multiplier on the number of mobs in a long saved-up (large) raid.
Max attackers at once in a medium raid
During a medium raid, the most attackers around a base at the same time.
Most mobs in one normal raid. 0 = no cap.
Most mobs in total in one medium raid. 0 = no cap.
Most mobs in total in one large raid. 0 = no cap (as many as were saved up).
During raids, strong mobs break walls and terrain to get through. When off they do not (they never do if the mobGriefing game rule is off).
Before a large raid, the forest goes quiet and stops spawning for a while. When off, large raids come without warning.
Multiplies the caps on mobs spawning naturally at the forest edge and underground. At 0% none spawn naturally (nurseries and raids are separate).
When on, animals, villagers and others killed by spores or plant-side mobs become parasitized forms or sprouts. When off they do not. Does not affect players.
When on, G3 mobs grow resistant to attacks used often against them. When off they do not (what they learned is kept and applies again when turned back on).
When off, fatigue does not build up and has no effect.
When on, your infection stage and its progress stay when you die and respawn. Exposure and fatigue start from 0. When off, dying cures it. Choosing Nightmare turns this on.
How slowly push-back tools wear out. At 200%, ash-and-lime bands stop twice as many times, ley stakes use half the FE and vent filters clog half as fast. Ranges do not change.
How often world events happen. 200% halves the gap (from the next event).
A large earthquake and fissure at the start of phase 1. When off it does not happen (the phase still starts).
When off, the quake only shakes and erupts spores without tearing the ground. Whether raids break walls is set in the Raids section.
When distant hordes come close and become real mobs, the most that can be real at once. Higher is heavier.
The most mobs in distant hordes (drawn as stand-ins).
When off, every horde is made of real mobs (heavier).
gui.overgrown_vegetation.visual_settings: Keeps drawing this mod's effects (light, fog, particles) while an Iris shader pack is in use. Some shader packs may show them broken or run slower.
Calls of jungle insects (crickets and others) and reptiles. Off also stops calls already playing. Barely affects performance.
Wind moving through the canopy. Off also stops the sound already playing. Barely affects performance.
Dripping water, creaking roots and the hum of spore pools underground in the overgrown region. Silent while the cave light is off. Barely affects performance.
A muffled low sound while diving in overgrown rivers, ponds and seas. Turns the vanilla underwater ambience down there. Barely affects performance.
Light shafts through the canopy and the glowing motes floating in them. Affects performance.
Spots of sunlight on the forest floor and their faint rays. Slightly affects performance.

Lifts the light on the floor of dense forest and adds green bounce light, and canopy shade and tint. Off returns the floor to vanilla darkness and also hides the sunfleck spots on the ground (they are drawn with the shade map). Slightly affects performance.
Spore fog in the forest and morning mist (terrain fog, fog distance and colour, Distant Horizons fog override, giant tree silhouettes beyond the fog). Affects performance.
Patchiness and light inside the fog (ray marching). Drawn only at Atmosphere Quality High. Strongly affects performance (the heaviest effect).
Falling leaves, drifting glowing spores, dusk motes, after-rain drops and steam. Affects performance.
Gnat swarms, and bugs bursting out of tree hollows and eyes inside them. Barely affects performance.
Leaves and grass sway in the wind (moved inside the terrain shader). Slightly affects performance.
Rings and bubbles on water and the sheen of wet ground. Slightly affects performance.
Caustics on the bottom, light shafts under water and glowing algae at night. Slightly affects performance.
Under the overgrown forest, only the glow of plants floats in black fog (point lights, mobs lit too). Prototype.
A soft glow around torches, lava, glowing plants and spores in the dark. A full-screen pass; turn it off if the game runs slow.
Under a low sun, bark and rock get relief from the light and dark of their textures. It assumes 16x16 textures, so resource packs with larger textures may show seams.
Soft shade on the forest floor, at the foot of trunks, in wall corners and where plants meet the ground. Two full-screen passes every frame, so it costs performance.
How many eyes open around the screen edge while a Phyllosens watchtower watches you (100% = all). 0% shows no eyes.
While watched, now and then an eye opens for a moment near the crosshair.
While watched, the dark screen edge throbs like a heartbeat.
Draw plant-side mobs of the same kind together on the GPU (GPU skinning). Hordes of hundreds become much lighter. Turn off only if mobs look wrong.
How far hordes are drawn before they become real mobs. Combined = rough models nearer, flat pictures beyond; Pictures = flat pictures only (lightest); Models = rough models only.

research.overgrown_vegetation.title: Research Bench - Research Tree
research.overgrown_vegetation.unknown_de: Research the earlier nodes to find out.

research.overgrown_vegetation.bench.name: Research Bench
research.overgrown_vegetation.bench.desc: Studies the specimens you bring back, powered by the ley lines. Pay specimens, ley power and time to open a node and its recipes.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t1_fiber.d: Fiber grass from the fringe twists into strong fiber for cloth, cord and bowstrings.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t1_armor.d: Cloth and leather expedition gear. Less armor than iron, but slows spore exposure, makes filters last and never weighs you down.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t1_knife.d: A blade that also cuts a path through vines and undergrowth.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t1_bow.des: Arrows tipped with roasted spores burn and smoulder where they hit. Strong against the forest.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t2_lens.de: An instrument for tier 2 specimens. Place it near the bench to study forest floor specimens. The gate to the next tier.
A copper and lime wash that briefly withers the forest's undergrowth and ground fungus. It grows back once spores settle again.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t3_resonat: An instrument for tier 3 specimens. It resonates ley power to study deep forest specimens. Place it near the bench with the Lens and Still.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t2_ore.des: Mycelium in the rock draws metal together with ley power. Found only in corrupted rock under ley lines.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t2_armor.d: As hard as diamond and fairly spore-proof (less than tier 1). Armor for fighting swarms head-on.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t2_sword.d: Cuts several enemies in the half circle ahead at once. Slow swing.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t2_xbow.de: A heavy bolt pierces a line of enemies. Slow to load.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t3_crystal: Store ley power in crystals grown by the forest root organs. The power source for armor and weapons, charged from your base batteries.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t3_armor.d: Regeneration and other buffs, no knockback and no fall damage. Runs on crystal power; armor stays when it runs out.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t3_heat.de: Burns as it cuts. Also burns vines and spore sacs.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t3_staff.d: Fires ley power. The bolt bursts and throws enemies back.
research.overgrown_vegetation.t3_tube.de: Short-range flame that burns a cone ahead. Also pushes back corruption.
